_comment: DESIGN.md §9. Nine normal monsters spanning all four armour types, plus four bosses - one per armour type, drawn at random on boss waves (§3.4). FIVE of the nine carry an ability and four do not: a wave whose every member is special is a wave with nothing special in it, so the cheap bodies stay cheap and the ones worth recognising are the ones a defence has to answer differently. Every boss has one, and three of the four are thresholds - wounding it is what sets it off. `range` is reach measured EDGE TO EDGE, so a melee value near zero means walking up and touching. `bodyRadius` is both the collision size and the drawn size. All placeholders.

bosses.name: Brood Sire
bosses._note: §3.4, amended. The bank is FOUR BODIES OF EQUAL POWER in four armour types, not a difficulty ladder: a boss is drawn at random, so a bank whose members ran 1,400 to 3,100 HP made wave 5 a different fight depending on the die. What makes wave 25's boss harder than wave 5's is waves.bossScaling, applied per BOSS WAVE. They still differ in shape - the ward one hits hardest and has least health, the flesh one the reverse - so which comes up changes how you fight it and not whether you can. Still single-armour, which §3.4 wants fixed with a multi-part boss model that does not exist yet.
